plain_english_revision: The amendment by Nathaniel Ledbetter to SB227 (Pharmacy Benefits Managers regulation) carves out exemptions for self-funded health plans governed by ERISA from certain state-level pharmacy benefit manager regulations. It also clarifies that specialty tier medications—including those eligible under CMS criteria—are subject to the law regardless of conflicting local rules.
candidate_position_supported: Advances policy effect: *Exempts ERISA-governed self-funded plans from state-mandated PBM transparency and fiduciary requirements.*
evidence_quotes: The following provisions shall not apply to the administration by a person of any term, including prescription drug benefits, of a self-funded health benefit plan that is governed by the federal Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974...
Subdivisions (1) and (5) of Sections 27-45A-8. ... Subdivisions (2), (3), (6), and (7) of Section 27-45A-10.

including each and every prescription medication that is eligible for specialty tier placement by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services pursuant to 42 C.F.R. § 423.560, regardless of any provision of law to the contrary
review_reason: The amendment text is clear on its intent: it removes specific state regulations from ERISA plans and expands CMS-defined specialty tiers. No hidden assumptions about broader ideology are made.
